83.h: 79 - Ṣafwān ibn Bayḍāʾ Abū ʿAmr al-Qurashī al-Fihrī *
83.t:
She is his mother.
Her name: Daʿd (1) bint Jaḥdam al-Fihriyyah.
And his father: he is Wahb ibn Rabīʿah ibn Hilāl ibn Mālik ibn Ḍabbah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr ibn Mālik, Abū ʿAmr al-Qurashī, al-Fihrī.
One of the Emigrants; he witnessed Badr.
فروى: الواقدي، عن محرز (2) بن جعفر، عن جعفر بن عمرو، قال:
Ṭuʿaymah ibn ʿAdī killed Ṣafwān ibn Bayḍāʾ.
Then al-Wāqidī said: This is one report.
And it has been reported to us that Ṣafwān ibn Bayḍāʾ was not killed on the day of Badr, and that he witnessed the battles.
He died in Ramaḍān, in the year 38 AH, and left no offspring (3) .
His brother:

84.h: 80 - Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ al-Fihrī Abū Mūsā**
84.t:
One of the Emigrants.
His patronymic (الكنية) was Abū Mūsā.
He made both emigrations to Abyssinia, according to the report of Ibn Isḥāq and al-Wāqidī. ⟦1:384⟧
And from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah, who said:
When Suhayl and Ṣafwān, the two sons of Bayḍāʾ, emigrated from Mecca, they stayed with Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm (1) .
Ibn Saʿd said: They said: Suhayl witnessed Badr when he was aged 34, and witnessed Uḥud ...
until he said: And he died in Medina in the year 9 AH, after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Tabūk, and left no offspring (2) .
I say: He is the one over whom the Prophet ﷺ prayed in the mosque (3) .
The two of them had a brother named Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ al-Fihrī, who witnessed Badr and witnessed Uḥud.

85.h: 81 - al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Mālik al-Kindī * (ع)
85.t:
A companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one of the first forerunners.
He is al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿah al-Quḍāʿī, al-Kindī, al-Bahrānī.
He is also called: al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad; because he was raised in the care of al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth ⟦1:385⟧ al-Zuhrī, who adopted him.
And it was said: rather he was a slave of his, black in colour, and he adopted him.
And it is said: rather he shed blood in Kindah, fled to Mecca, and made a pact with al-Aswad.
He witnessed Badr and the other battles, and it is established that he was a horseman on the day of Badr, while there was disagreement that day about al-Zubayr.
He has a number of hadiths.
Narrating from him: علي، وابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وجبير بن نفير، وابن أبي ليلى، وهمام بن الحارث، وعبيد الله بن عدي بن الخيار، وجماعة.
And it was said: he was dark-complexioned, tall, big-bellied, thick-haired, wide-eyed, with joined eyebrows, awe-inspiring.
He lived about seventy years.
He died in the year 33 AH, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān prayed over him, and his grave is at al-Baqīʿ (may Allah be pleased with him) (1) .
His hadith is in (the Six Books (الكتب الستة)): he has a hadith in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين) (2)), and Muslim alone transmitted four hadiths of his (3) . ⟦1:386⟧
أخبرنا إسحاق الأسدي، أنبأنا ابن خليل، أنبأنا اللبان، أنبأنا أبو علي الحداد، أنبأنا أبو نعيم، أنبأنا أحمد بن المسندي، حدثنا موسى بن هارون، حدثنا عباس بن الوليد، حدثنا بشر بن المفضل، حدثنا ابن عون، عن عمير بن إسحاق، عن المقداد بن الأسود، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me over a task ⟦1:387⟧ .
When I returned, he said: (How did you find authority?) .
I said: O Messenger of Allah! I thought nothing other than that the people were all my servants; by Allah, I will never take charge of any task as long as I live (1) .
بقية: حدثنا حريز بن عثمان، حدثني عبد الرحمن بن ميسرة، حدثني أبو راشد الحبراني، قال:
I met al-Miqdād, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in Ḥimṣ, sitting on one of the chests of the money-changers, over which his bulk overflowed, as he intended to go on a military expedition.
I said to him: Allah has excused you.
He said: The sūrah of the Buḥūth has refused us: “March forth, whether light or heavy” [al-Tawbah (2) : 41] .
يحيى الحماني: حدثنا ابن المبارك، عن صفوان بن عمرو، حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن جبير بن نفير، عن أبيه، قال:
We sat with al-Miqdād one day, and a man passed by him and said:
Blessed are these two eyes that saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; by Allah, we wish we had seen what you saw.
I listened and began to wonder; he had said nothing but good.
Then al-Miqdād turned to him and said:
What leads one of you to wish for an occasion that Allah has kept hidden from him, not knowing how he would have fared had he witnessed it? By Allah, there were present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ people whom Allah cast on their faces into Hell; they did not answer him (3) , and did not believe him.
Do you not praise Allah, that you do not ⟦1:388⟧ know any but your Lord, believing in what your Prophet brought, having been spared the trial by others?
By Allah, the Prophet ﷺ was sent in the hardest condition in which any prophet was ever sent, in a time of interval between messengers and of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), when they saw no religion better than the worship of idols; so he came with a Criterion, until a man would see his father, or his son, or his brother a disbeliever, while Allah had opened the lock of his heart to faith, so that he knew that whoever entered the Fire had perished; his eye is not comforted while he knows that his close kin is in the Fire. And it is of this that Allah the Exalted said: “Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring comfort to our eyes” [al-Furqān (1) : 74] .
And in (Musnad Aḥmad), from Buraydah:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Hold fast to love of four: ʿAlī, Abū Dharr, Salmān, and al-Miqdād (2)) .
And from Karīmah bint al-Miqdād: that al-Miqdād bequeathed to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn thirty-six thousand, and to each of the Mothers of the Believers seven thousand dirhams.
And it was said: he drank castor oil and died.
